newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany to tax life insurance payouts - magazine.
newsitem.headline: Germany to tax life insurance payouts - magazine.

text.p: Germany is planning to introduce tax on certain forms of life insurance, Focus magazine reported on Saturday, citing sources in the government's tax reform committee.

In an advance summary of an article to be released this week, Focus said that 30 percent of income from life insurance policies that pay out monthly would in the future be classified as liable for tax.
The committee had agreed on this measure last week, Focus said. It was unclear whether existing life insurance contracts would be affected.

Separately, the Spiegel magazine reported that the government aimed to tackle the problem of an ageing population by gradually reducing the level of pension payments to 63 percent of ordinary net income from the current 70 percent.

Spiegel said the plan, devised by a committee headed by Labour Minister Norbert Bluem and running through to the year 2030, would ensure that pension contributions would not exceed 22 percent in the decades to come.
The reductions would affect in particular individuals who retire early on health grounds, Spiegel said.
No immediate confirmation of the reports was available.
